summary: In this concise 45-second excerpt, Jeanne Bliss recalls leaving Microsoft in 2002 and writing what she calls the first practical guide to customer experience, Chief Customer Officer. She notes she had to convince the publisher to name the book after the emerging role, and observes that the book quickly provided a roadmap for practitioners—supporting her view that the Chief Customer Officer role was just beginning to be considered. BlissThen frames the idea of “brave Crusaders” tackling the customer gauntlet, positioning the book as foundational guidance for organizations seeking to formalize customer-centric leadership.
title: Chief Customer Officer: Defining a Leadership Role for Customer Experience
topics: publication and naming of a new role
